sanskrit: etad dhi tritayaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvabhūteṣu bhārata nirvairatā mahārāja satyam adroha eva ca
english: For these three, O Bhārata, are the highest among all creatures: freedom from enmity, O great king, truthfulness, and the absence of malice.

sanskrit: kaccit te nānutāpo 'sti vanavāsena bhārata svadate vanyaṃ annaṃ vā munivāsāṃsi vā vibho
english: You feel no regret, I trust, O Bhārata, at this dwelling in the forest? Does the wild food please you, O lord, and the garments of the sages?

sanskrit: viditaṃ cāpi me rājan vidurasya mahātmanaḥ gamanaṃ vidhinā yena dharmasya sumahātmanaḥ
english: And known to me as well, O king, is the departure of the high-souled Vidura, by what ordinance he, who was the great-souled Dharma himself, passed away.

sanskrit: māṇḍavyaśāpād dhi sa vai dharmo viduratāṃ gataḥ mahābuddhir mahāyogī mahātmā sumahāmanāḥ
english: For by the curse of Māṇḍavya did Dharma indeed enter into the state of Vidura—he of great wisdom, the mighty yogin, the great-souled one, exceedingly noble of mind.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir vā deveṣu śukro vāpy asureṣu yaḥ na tathā buddhisaṃpanno yathā sa puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Neither Bṛhaspati among the gods, nor Śukra among the asuras, was so endowed with intellect as that bull among men.

sanskrit: tapobalavyayaṃ kṛtvā sumahac cirasaṃbhṛtam māṇḍavyenarṣiṇā dharmo hy abhibhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Expending a vast store of ascetic power long accumulated, the sage Māṇḍavya overpowered the eternal Dharma himself.

sanskrit: niyogād brahmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ mayā svena balena ca vaicitravīryake kṣetre jātaḥ sa sumahāmatiḥ
english: By the command of Brahmā of old, and by my own power, that one of exceeding wisdom was born in the field of Vicitravīrya.

sanskrit: bhrātā tava mahārāja devadevaḥ sanātanaḥ dhāraṇāc chreyaso dhyānād yaṃ dharmaṃ kavayo viduḥ
english: Your brother, O great king, was the eternal god of gods—that Dharma whom the seers know by reason of his upholding the good and his meditation.

sanskrit: satyena saṃvardhayati damena niyamena ca ahiṃsayā ca dānena tapasā ca sanātanaḥ
english: By truth he increases it, and by self-restraint and by discipline, by non-injury and by giving and by austerity—he, the eternal one.

sanskrit: yena yogabalāj jātaḥ kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dharma ity eṣa nṛpate prājñenāmitabuddhinā
english: By whom, through the power of yoga, the Kuru king Yudhiṣṭhira was begotten—this is Dharma, O king, by that wise one of boundless intellect.

sanskrit: yathā hy agnir yathā vāyur yathāpaḥ pṛthivī yathā yathākāśaṃ tathā dharma iha cāmutra ca sthitaḥ
english: As fire, as wind, as the waters, as earth, as ether—so does Dharma abide, both here and in the world beyond.

sanskrit: sarvagaś caiva kauravya sarvaṃ vyāpya carācaram dṛśyate devadevaḥ sa siddhair nirdagdhakilbiṣaiḥ
english: All-pervading, O Kaurava, pervading the whole world of moving and unmoving things, that god of gods is seen by the perfected ones whose sins have been burned away.

sanskrit: yo hi dharmaḥ sa viduro viduro yaḥ sa pāṇḍavaḥ sa eṣa rājan vaśyas te pāṇḍavaḥ preṣyavat sthitaḥ
english: For he who is Dharma, he is Vidura; and he who is Vidura, he is the Pāṇḍava. This Pāṇḍava, O king, stood subject to you, ready like a servant.

sanskrit: praviṣṭaḥ sa svam ātmānaṃ bhrātā te buddhisattamaḥ diṣṭyā mahātmā kaunteyaṃ mahāyogabalānvitaḥ
english: He has entered into his own self—your brother, best in wisdom; by good fortune the great-souled one, endowed with the great power of yoga, has passed into the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: tvāṃ cāpi śreyasā yokṣye nacirād bharatarṣabha saṃśayacchedanārthaṃ hi prāptaṃ māṃ viddhi putraka
english: You too I shall soon join with what is good, O bull of the Bhāratas; know me, dear child, to have come for the cutting away of doubt.

sanskrit: na kṛtaṃ yat purā kaiś cit karma loke maharṣibhiḥ āścaryabhūtaṃ tapasaḥ phalaṃ saṃdarśayāmi vaḥ
english: A deed that no great seers in the world have ever wrought before—a marvel, the fruit of austerity—this I shall reveal to you all.

sanskrit: kim icchasi mahīpāla mattaḥ prāptum amānuṣam draṣṭuṃ spraṣṭum atha śrotuṃ vada kartāsmi tat tathā
english: What more than human thing do you wish to obtain from me, O protector of the earth—to see, to touch, or to hear? Speak, and I shall make it so.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca vanavāsaṃ gate vipra dhṛtarāṣṭre mahīpatau sabhārye nṛpaśārdūle vadhvā kuntyā samanvite
english: Janamejaya said: When the lord of the earth Dhṛtarāṣṭra had gone, O brāhmaṇa, to dwell in the forest—that tiger among kings, together with his wife and accompanied by his daughter-in-law Kuntī—

sanskrit: vidure cāpi saṃsiddhe dharmarājaṃ vyapāśrite vasatsu pāṇḍuputreṣu sarveṣv āśramamaṇḍale
english: and when Vidura too had attained perfection, merging into the Dharma King, while all the sons of Pāṇḍu dwelt within the circle of the hermitage—

sanskrit: yat tad āścaryam iti vai kariṣyāmīty uvāca ha vyāsaḥ paramatejasvī maharṣis tad vadasva me
english: that marvel which Vyāsa of supreme splendor, the great seer, said he would perform—tell that to me.

sanskrit: vanavāse ca kauravyaḥ kiyantaṃ kālam acyutaḥ yudhiṣṭhiro narapatir nyavasat sajano dvija
english: And how long a time did the Kaurava, the unwavering king of men Yudhiṣṭhira, dwell in the forest with his people, O brāhmaṇa?

sanskrit: kimāhārāś ca te tatra sasainyā nyavasan prabho sāntaḥpurā mahātmāna iti tad brūhi me 'nagha
english: On what food did those great-souled ones live there, with their army and the women of the inner apartments, O lord? Tell me that, O sinless one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te 'nujñātās tadā rājan kururājena pāṇḍavāḥ vividhāny annapānāni viśrāmyānubhavanti te
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Granted leave then, O king, by the Kuru king, the Pāṇḍavas, resting, partook of food and drink of various kinds.

sanskrit: māsam ekaṃ vijahrus te sasainyāntaḥpurā vane atha tatrāgamad vyāso yathoktaṃ te mayānagha
english: For one month they dwelt there in the forest, with their army and their women; then Vyāsa came to that place, as I have told you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: tathā tu teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ kathābhir nṛpasaṃnidhau vyāsam anvāsatāṃ rājann ājagmur munayo 'pare
english: And as they all sat there in the king's presence with their talk, attending upon Vyāsa, O king, other sages too arrived.

sanskrit: nāradaḥ parvataś caiva devalaś ca mahātapāḥ viśvāvasus tumburuś ca citrasenaś ca bhārata
english: Nārada and Parvata and Devala of great austerity, and Viśvāvasu and Tumburu and Citrasena, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: teṣām api yathānyāyaṃ pūjāṃ cakre mahāmanāḥ dhṛtarāṣṭrābhyanujñātaḥ kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: To them too, in due form, the noble-minded Kuru king Yudhiṣṭhira, with Dhṛtarāṣṭra's leave, paid honor.

sanskrit: niṣedus te tataḥ sarve pūjāṃ prāpya yudhiṣṭhirāt āsaneṣv atha puṇyeṣu barhiṣkeṣu vareṣu ca
english: Then, having received honor from Yudhiṣṭhira, they all sat down upon holy seats and upon excellent cushions of kuśa grass.

sanskrit: teṣu tatropaviṣṭeṣu sa tu rājā mahāmatiḥ pāṇḍuputraiḥ parivṛto niṣasāda kurūdvahaḥ
english: When they had taken their seats there, that king of great wisdom, the upholder of the Kurus, surrounded by the sons of Pāṇḍu, sat down.

sanskrit: gāndhārī caiva kuntī ca draupadī sātvatī tathā striyaś cānyās tathānyābhiḥ sahopaviviśus tataḥ
english: Gāndhārī and Kuntī, and Draupadī and the Sātvatī woman, and the other women too then sat down together with still others.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tatra kathā divyā dharmiṣṭhāś cābhavan nṛpa ṛṣīṇāṃ ca purāṇānāṃ devāsuravimiśritāḥ
english: Their talk there became celestial and most righteous, O king, and of the ancient seers, mingled with tales of gods and asuras.

sanskrit: tataḥ kathānte vyāsas taṃ prajñācakṣuṣam īśvaram provāca vadatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ punar eva sa tad vacaḥ prīyamāṇo mahātejāḥ sarvavedavidāṃ varaḥ
english: Then, at the close of the talk, Vyāsa, best of speakers, of great splendor, foremost of all who know the Vedas, well pleased, spoke once more those words to that lord whose eye was wisdom.

sanskrit: viditaṃ mama rājendra yat te hṛdi vivakṣitam dahyamānasya śokena tava putrakṛtena vai
english: Known to me is it, O king of kings, what you wish to utter in your heart, you who are consumed by the grief brought on by your sons.

sanskrit: gāndhāryāś caiva yad duḥkhaṃ hṛdi tiṣṭhati pārthiva kuntyāś ca yan mahārāja draupadyāś ca hṛdi sthitam
english: And the sorrow that abides in Gāndhārī's heart, O king, and that which dwells in the heart of Kuntī, O great king, and in Draupadī's—

sanskrit: yac ca dhārayate tīvraṃ duḥkhaṃ putravināśajam subhadrā kṛṣṇabhaginī tac cāpi viditaṃ mama
english: and the keen grief born of her son's destruction that Subhadrā, Kṛṣṇa's sister, bears—that too is known to me.

sanskrit: śrutvā samāgamam imaṃ sarveṣāṃ vas tato nṛpa saṃśayacchedanāyāhaṃ prāptaḥ kauravanandana
english: Having heard of this gathering of you all, O king, I have come for the cutting away of doubt, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: ime ca devagandharvāḥ sarve caiva maharṣayaḥ paśyantu tapaso vīryam adya me cirasaṃbhṛtam
english: And let these gods and gandharvas, and all the great seers, behold today the might of my austerity, long stored up.

sanskrit: tad ucyatāṃ mahābāho kaṃ kāmaṃ pradiśāmi te pravaṇo 'smi varaṃ dātuṃ paśya me tapaso balam
english: Therefore let it be told, O mighty-armed one, what desire I may grant you; I am inclined to give a boon—behold the power of my austerity.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa rājendro vyāsenāmitabuddhinā muhūrtam iva saṃcintya vacanāyopacakrame
english: Thus addressed by Vyāsa of boundless intellect, that king of kings, after pondering for a moment, set himself to speak.

sanskrit: dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ ca me yan me samāgamo 'dyeha bhavadbhiḥ saha sādhubhiḥ
english: Blessed am I, favored am I, and fruitful is my life, in that today I have here this meeting with you, the holy ones.

sanskrit: adya cāpy avagacchāmi gatim iṣṭām ihātmanaḥ bhavadbhir brahmakalpair yat sameto 'haṃ tapodhanāḥ
english: And today too I perceive the desired destiny of my soul, in that I am united with you, who are like unto Brahmā, O you whose wealth is austerity.

sanskrit: darśanād eva bhavatāṃ pūto 'haṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ vidyate na bhayaṃ cāpi paralokān mamānaghāḥ
english: By the mere sight of you I am made pure—of this there is no doubt; nor is there any fear in me from the world beyond, O sinless ones.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu tasya sudurbuddher mandasyāpanayair bhṛśam dūyate me mano nityaṃ smarataḥ putragṛddhinaḥ
english: Yet my mind is ever sorely tormented by the misdeeds of that dull-witted, foolish son of mine, who was greedy and grasping, whenever I remember him.

sanskrit: apāpāḥ pāṇḍavā yena nikṛtāḥ pāpabuddhinā ghātitā pṛthivī ceyaṃ sahasā sanaradvipā
english: By whom, of wicked mind, the innocent Pāṇḍavas were wronged, and this earth with its men and elephants was suddenly brought to slaughter—

sanskrit: rājānaś ca mahātmāno nānājanapadeśvarāḥ āgamya mama putrārthe sarve mṛtyuvaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: and great-souled kings, lords of diverse realms, having come for my son's sake, all passed into the power of death.

sanskrit: ye te putrāṃś ca dārāś ca prāṇāṃś ca manasaḥ priyān parityajya gatāḥ śūrāḥ pretarājaniveśanam
english: Those heroes who, forsaking their sons and wives and their lives, dear to their hearts, went to the abode of the king of the dead—

sanskrit: kā nu teṣāṃ gatir brahman mitrārthe ye hatā mṛdhe tathaiva putrapautrāṇāṃ mama ye nihatā yudhi
english: what now is the destiny, O brāhmaṇa, of those who were slain in battle for a friend's sake, and likewise of those of my sons and grandsons who were killed in the fight?

sanskrit: dūyate me mano 'bhīkṣṇaṃ ghātayitvā mahābalam bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ vṛddhaṃ droṇaṃ ca dvijasattamam
english: My mind is tormented again and again at having caused the slaying of the mighty Bhīṣma, the aged son of Śaṃtanu, and Droṇa, that best of brāhmaṇas—

sanskrit: mama putreṇa mūḍhena pāpena suhṛdadviṣā kṣayaṃ nītaṃ kulaṃ dīptaṃ pṛthivīrājyam icchatā
english: by my son, deluded and wicked, a hater of his own friends, who, coveting the kingdom of the earth, brought our illustrious house to ruin.

sanskrit: etat sarvam anusmṛtya dahyamāno divāniśam na śāntim adhigacchāmi duḥkhaśokasamāhataḥ iti me cintayānasya pitaḥ śarma na vidyate
english: Remembering all this, burning day and night, I find no peace, stricken by pain and grief; for me, brooding thus, O father, there is no comfort to be found.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tac chrutvā vividhaṃ tasya rājarṣeḥ paridevitam punar navīkṛtaḥ śoko gāndhāryā janamejaya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the manifold lamentation of that royal sage, the grief of Gāndhārī was renewed, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: kuntyā drupadaputryāś ca subhadrāyās tathaiva ca tāsāṃ ca varanārīṇāṃ vadhūnāṃ kauravasya ha
english: And of Kuntī, and of Drupada's daughter, and likewise of Subhadrā, and of those noble women, the brides of the Kaurava house.

sanskrit: putraśokasamāviṣṭā gāndhārī tv idam abravīt śvaśuraṃ baddhanayanā devī prāñjalir utthitā
english: Overwhelmed by grief for her sons, Gāndhārī, the queen with bound eyes, rose with joined palms and spoke this to her father-in-law:

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśemāni varṣāṇi gatāni munipuṃgava asya rājño hatān putrāñ śocato na śamo vibho
english: These sixteen years have passed, O bull among sages, yet for this king, grieving for his slain sons, there is no peace, O lord.

sanskrit: putraśokasamāviṣṭo niḥśvasan hy eṣa bhūmipaḥ na śete vasatīḥ sarvā dhṛtarāṣṭro mahāmune
english: Overwhelmed with grief for his sons, sighing, this lord of the earth, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, sleeps not through all the nights, O great sage.

sanskrit: lokān anyān samartho 'si sraṣṭuṃ sarvāṃs tapobalāt kim u lokāntaragatān rājño darśayituṃ sutān
english: You are able to create whole other worlds by the power of your austerity; how much more, then, to show the king his sons who have gone to another world?

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca draupadī kṛṣṇā hatajñātisutā bhṛśam śocaty atīva sādhvī te snuṣāṇāṃ dayitā snuṣā
english: And this Kṛṣṇā, Draupadī, whose kinsmen and sons were slain, grieves exceedingly—the virtuous one, the dearest of your daughters-in-law.

sanskrit: tathā kṛṣṇasya bhaginī subhadrā bhadrabhāṣiṇī saubhadravadhasaṃtaptā bhṛśaṃ śocati bhāminī
english: So too Kṛṣṇa's sister Subhadrā, sweet of speech, scorched by the slaying of Saubhadra, grieves greatly, the lovely woman.

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca bhūriśravaso bhāryā paramaduḥkhitā bhartṛvyasanaśokārtā na śete vasatīḥ prabho
english: And this wife of Bhūriśravas, most sorely afflicted, tormented by grief at her husband's calamity, sleeps not through the nights, O lord.

sanskrit: yasyās tu śvaśuro dhīmān bāhlīkaḥ sa kurūdvahaḥ nihataḥ somadattaś ca pitrā saha mahāraṇe
english: Whose father-in-law, the wise Bāhlīka, upholder of the Kurus, was slain, and Somadatta together with his father, in the great battle.

sanskrit: śrīmac cāsya mahābuddheḥ saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinaḥ putrasya te putraśataṃ nihataṃ yad raṇājire
english: And the hundred sons of your son—he the illustrious, of great wisdom, who never fled in battles—who were slain on the field of war.

sanskrit: tasya bhāryāśatam idaṃ putraśokasamāhatam punaḥ punar vardhayānaṃ śokaṃ rājño mamaiva ca tenārambheṇa mahatā mām upāste mahāmune
english: This hundred wives of his, stricken with grief for their sons, again and again increasing the sorrow of the king and of myself, with that great undertaking attends upon me, O great sage.

sanskrit: ye ca śūrā mahātmānaḥ śvaśurā me mahārathāḥ somadattaprabhṛtayaḥ kā nu teṣāṃ gatiḥ prabho
english: And those heroes, the great-souled mighty charioteers, my fathers-in-law, Somadatta and the rest—what now is their destiny, O lord?

sanskrit: tava prasādād bhagavan viśoko 'yaṃ mahīpatiḥ kuryāt kālam ahaṃ caiva kuntī ceyaṃ vadhūs tava
english: By your grace, O blessed one, may this lord of the earth pass his time free from grief, and I as well, and this Kuntī, your daughter-in-law.

sanskrit: ity uktavatyāṃ gāndhāryāṃ kuntī vratakṛśānanā pracchannajātaṃ putraṃ taṃ sasmārādityasaṃbhavam
english: When Gāndhārī had thus spoken, Kuntī, her face wasted by vows, remembered that son of hers, secretly born, sprung from the Sun.

sanskrit: tām ṛṣir varado vyāso dūraśravaṇadarśanaḥ apaśyad duḥkhitāṃ devīṃ mātaraṃ savyasācinaḥ
english: That boon-granting sage Vyāsa, of far-reaching hearing and sight, beheld her grieving, the queen, the mother of Savyasācin.

sanskrit: tām uvāca tato vyāso yat te kāryaṃ vivakṣitam tad brūhi tvaṃ mahāprājñe yat te manasi vartate
english: Then Vyāsa said to her: Whatever matter you wish to speak of, tell it, O most wise one, that which abides in your mind.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuntī śvaśurayoḥ praṇamya śirasā tadā uvāca vākyaṃ savrīḍaṃ vivṛṇvānā purātanam
english: Then Kuntī, bowing her head to her two elders, spoke with shame these words, disclosing a thing of long ago.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca bhagavañ śvaśuro me 'si daivatasyāpi daivatam sa me devātidevas tvaṃ śṛṇu satyāṃ giraṃ mama
english: Kuntī said: O blessed one, you are my father-in-law, the deity even of deities; you are to me the god above gods—hear my truthful word.

sanskrit: tapasvī kopano vipro durvāsā nāma me pituḥ bhikṣām upāgato bhoktuṃ tam ahaṃ paryatoṣayam
english: An ascetic, an irascible brāhmaṇa, Durvāsas by name, came to my father's house to take alms and eat; him I fully satisfied.

sanskrit: śaucena tv āgasas tyāgaiḥ śuddhena manasā tathā kopasthāneṣv api mahatsv akupyaṃ na kadā cana
english: By purity, by the avoidance of offense, and with a cleansed mind, even on great occasions for anger I never grew angry at any time.

sanskrit: sa me varam adāt prītaḥ kṛtam ity aham abruvam avaśyaṃ te grahītavyam iti māṃ so 'bravīd vacaḥ
english: He, well pleased, granted me a boon; "It is enough," said I, but he spoke this word to me: "It must surely be received by you."

sanskrit: tataḥ śāpabhayād vipram avocaṃ punar eva tam evam astv iti ca prāha punar eva sa māṃ dvijaḥ
english: Then, for fear of a curse, I said to the brāhmaṇa once again, "So be it"; and that twice-born one spoke to me once more:

sanskrit: dharmasya jananī bhadre bhavitrī tvaṃ varānane vaśe sthāsyanti te devā yāṃs tvam āvāhayiṣyasi
english: "You shall be the mother of righteousness, O gracious one, O fair-faced lady; those gods whom you summon shall stand subject to you."

sanskrit: ity uktvāntarhito vipras tato 'haṃ vismitābhavam na ca sarvāsv avasthāsu smṛtir me vipraṇaśyati
english: Having said this, the brāhmaṇa vanished; then I was filled with wonder, and in all conditions thereafter my memory of it never faded.

sanskrit: atha harmyatalasthāhaṃ ravim udyantam īkṣatī saṃsmṛtya tad ṛṣer vākyaṃ spṛhayantī divākaram sthitāhaṃ bālabhāvena tatra doṣam abudhyatī
english: Then, standing upon the terrace of the palace, gazing at the rising sun, recalling that word of the sage, longing for the maker of day, I stood—in childish innocence not perceiving the fault therein.

sanskrit: atha devaḥ sahasrāṃśur matsamīpagato 'bhavat dvidhā kṛtvātmano dehaṃ bhūmau ca gagane 'pi ca tatāpa lokān ekena dvitīyenāgamac ca mām
english: Then the thousand-rayed god drew near to me; dividing his body in two, both on the earth and in the sky, with the one he warmed the worlds, and with the other he came to me.

sanskrit: sa mām uvāca vepantīṃ varaṃ matto vṛṇīṣva ha gamyatām iti taṃ cāhaṃ praṇamya śirasāvadam
english: He said to me, who was trembling, "Choose a boon from me, then let me go"; and I, bowing my head to him, spoke:

sanskrit: sa mām uvāca tigmāṃśur vṛthāhvānaṃ na te kṣamam dhakṣyāmi tvāṃ ca vipraṃ ca yena datto varas tava
english: The fierce-rayed one said to me, "A summoning in vain is not permitted you; I shall burn both you and the brāhmaṇa by whom this boon was given to you."

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ rakṣatī vipraṃ śāpād anaparādhinam putro me tvatsamo deva bhaved iti tato 'bruvam
english: Then I, seeking to shield the brāhmaṇa, who was guiltless, from a curse, said this: "Let there be born to me, O god, a son equal to you."
